Encode texts as sentence embeddings

Source: R/encode.R
encode.Rd

encode() returns one sentence embedding per text from a pinned model (see models()): a point in a vector space learned so that texts with similar meaning lie close together, whatever words they use. Sentence-BERT models (Reimers and Gurevych, 2019) obtain such a vector by running a transformer encoder over the text and pooling its token vectors; the cosine of the angle between two embeddings then measures how close the two texts are in meaning.

Each text is tokenized with the model's own tokenizer, truncated to the model's maximum length, run through the ONNX graph, pooled with the model's rule (pool()), and by default scaled to unit length. The static potion-base-8M model instead averages looked-up token vectors and needs no ONNX Runtime. With cache, embeddings are stored in a file keyed by text and model, so encoding an edited corpus again computes only the new or changed texts. The result is a numeric matrix with one row per text, in input order.

Encoding is the expensive step of a workflow, and every analysis in the package (topics, the assignment of new texts, similarity) starts from its result: encode once and pass the matrix to the embeddings argument of topics(), compare_topics(), topic_corpus(), predict(), representatives() and topic_gamma(). To split long documents into sentences or clauses first, use segment(). The bundled feedback_embeddings matrix is the output of encode() for 600 feedback messages and lets the examples run without a model.

Usage

encode(
  text,
  model = NULL,
  batch_size = 32L,
  normalize = TRUE,
  prefix = NULL,
  sort_by_length = FALSE,
  cache = NULL
)

Arguments

text

Character vector, one text per element. Empty strings are allowed; NA is not. Names become the row names of the result.

model

A model from load_model() or load_custom(), the name of a pinned model from models(), or NULL (default) for "all-MiniLM-L6-v2". A name is loaded once per session. A model that is not installed is downloaded only with consent: an interactive prompt, or options(sbert.download = TRUE) in a script.

batch_size

Number of texts per model call (default 32).

normalize

Scale each embedding to unit L2 length (default TRUE).

prefix

Text prepended to every input. NULL (default) uses the model's pinned prefix (for example "query: " for E5 models); "" uses none.

sort_by_length

Batch texts of similar length together, which reduces computation over padding, most of all for segments of varying length (default FALSE). The rows keep input order, but the values can differ from an unsorted run by floating-point rounding, enough to change the assignment of a rare unit on a topic boundary.

cache

NULL (default), or the path of an .rds file of stored embeddings. Texts already stored for the same model and settings are read from the file; the others are encoded once each (repeats within the call included) and added to it. A file that cannot be read, or was written for another embedding dimension, is rebuilt with a warning.

Value

A numeric matrix with one row per text, in input order, and one column per embedding dimension of the model (the dimensions column of models()). Row names are names(text). An empty text gives a matrix with no rows.

Conditions

sbert_unknown_model when model names no pinned model; sbert_model_not_installed when the model is not installed and its download is declined or not permitted; sbert_download_failed or sbert_cache_invalid when a permitted download fails or does not verify; sbert_cache_invalid when installed files fail verification; sbert_runtime_missing when ONNX Runtime is not installed; sbert_missing_package when the static model is loaded without jsonlite; sbert_model_error when the model cannot be loaded, or inference fails or returns non-finite values. Warning sbert_cache_rebuilt when the cache file is unusable.

References

Reimers, N., & Gurevych, I. (2019). Sentence-BERT: Sentence embeddings using Siamese BERT-networks. Proceedings of the 2019 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing and the 9th International Joint Conference on Natural Language Processing (EMNLP-IJCNLP), 3982-3992. doi:10.18653/v1/D19-1410

See also

load_model() and models() for the models; segment() to split documents first; topic_similarity() to compare embeddings; topics() to fit topics on them.

Examples

# The bundled embeddings are what encode() returns for 600 feedback
# messages: one row per text, one column per model dimension.
dim(feedback_embeddings)
#> [1] 600 384
topic_similarity(head(feedback_embeddings, 3))
#>            [,1]       [,2]       [,3]
#> [1,] 1.00000000 0.36132672 0.09539736
#> [2,] 0.36132672 1.00000000 0.09345878
#> [3,] 0.09539736 0.09345878 1.00000000

# \donttest{
if (interactive()) {
  model <- load_model()
  embeddings <- encode(c("A short sentence.", "Another sentence."), model)

  # Segment-level work benefits most, because segment lengths vary widely.
  segments <- with(head(covid, 50), segment(Abstract, level = "clause"))
  embeddings <- with(segments, encode(text, model, sort_by_length = TRUE))

  # Encode once, then re-run after editing the corpus: only changed rows cost
  # anything the second time.
  store <- file.path(tempdir(), "covid-embeddings.rds")
  embeddings <- with(covid, encode(Abstract, model, cache = store))
  embeddings <- with(covid, encode(Abstract, model, cache = store))
  unlink(store)
}
# }
